# STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 ESC: Power-Stage Loss Model, Thermal Budget, and Bi-Directional DShot600 Timer/DMA Allocation

## 0. Scope, Assumptions, and One Architectural Correction

**Correction on the 48 kHz switching.** The STM32H743 does not drive the MOSFET gates. It sends DShot600 frames to the 4-in-1 ESC. The 48 kHz PWM is generated by the ESC's own MCU (typically AT32F421, STM32G071, or EFM8 running AM32 or BLHeli_32/S). The model below keeps the two domains separate:

- **Domain A:** ESC power stage (losses, thermal).
- **Domain B:** FC digital link (DShot timers and DMA).

**No component BOM was supplied for Job #42**, so all numeric results use the representative parts in the table below. Every equation is parametric, so you can substitute datasheet values.

| Parameter | Symbol | Assumed value |
|---|---|---|
| Bus voltage (6S, full charge) | V_bus | 25.2 V |
| Burst current per motor channel | I | 80 A (10 s burst) |
| MOSFET (40 V, 3.3×3.3 DFN class) | R_ds(on),25 | 1.2 mΩ max @ V_gs = 10 V |
| R_ds(on) temperature coefficient | α | 0.0045 /K |
| Rise + fall time (with driver) | t_r + t_f | 20 ns |
| Output charge | Q_oss | 30 nC |
| Reverse recovery charge | Q_rr | 40 nC |
| Body-diode forward voltage | V_f | 0.8 V |
| Dead time | t_dt | 100 ns |
| Total gate charge | Q_g | 50 nC @ 10 V |
| PWM frequency | f_sw | 48 kHz |
| Junction-to-case thermal resistance | R_θJC | 1.5 K/W |
| Board | — | 30.5×30.5 mm, 6-layer, 2 oz Cu |

---

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

### 1.1 Current path

The model assumes 6-step trapezoidal commutation with synchronous (complementary) rectification, which is the AM32 and BLHeli_32 default.

During each 60° electrical sector:

- One high-side FET (H_x) is PWM'd at duty D.
- One low-side FET (L_y) is held fully on.
- During the off-time (1−D), the current freewheels through the complementary low-side FET L_x.

As a result, two FET channels are always in series with the motor current, regardless of duty cycle:

$$P_{cond,ch} = 2\,I_{ph,rms}^2\,R_{ds}(T_j)$$

$$R_{ds}(T_j) = R_{ds,25}\,[1+\alpha(T_j-25)]$$

### 1.2 Phase current vs. bus current

The relationship between average bus current and phase current is:

$$I_{bus} \approx D\cdot I_{ph}$$

The worst case is the 80 A burst at near-full throttle (D → 1), where I_ph ≈ I_bus ≈ 80 A. At partial throttle, phase current exceeds bus current. Keep this in mind for current-limit tuning.

### 1.3 Numeric result (T_j = 125 °C)

$$R_{ds} = 1.2\,\text{mΩ}\times(1+0.0045\times100) = 1.74\,\text{mΩ}$$

$$P_{cond,ch} = 2\times80^2\times1.74\times10^{-3} = \mathbf{22.3\ W\ per\ motor\ channel}$$

Over a full electrical cycle, each of the 6 FETs averages:

$$P_{cond,FET} \approx 22.3/6 \approx 3.7\,\text{W}$$

The instantaneous peak per FET is 11.1 W while it is conducting.

---

## 2. Switching Loss Model at 48 kHz

Only the PWM'd half-bridge leg incurs switching loss. Its components are:

$$P_{sw} = \underbrace{\tfrac12 V_{bus} I (t_r+t_f) f_{sw}}_{\text{V–I overlap}} + \underbrace{Q_{oss}V_{bus}f_{sw}}_{\text{C}_{oss}} + \underbrace{Q_{rr}V_{bus}f_{sw}}_{\text{reverse recovery}} + \underbrace{2V_f I t_{dt} f_{sw}}_{\text{dead-time diode}} + \underbrace{n\,Q_g V_{gs} f_{sw}}_{\text{gate drive}}$$

### 2.1 Loss breakdown per channel

| Term | Calculation | Loss |
|---|---|---|
| V–I overlap | 0.5 × 25.2 × 80 × 20 ns × 48 k | 0.968 W |
| C_oss | 30 nC × 25.2 × 48 k | 0.036 W |
| Q_rr | 40 nC × 25.2 × 48 k | 0.048 W |
| Dead-time diode | 2 × 0.8 × 80 × 100 ns × 48 k | 0.614 W |
| Gate drive (2 FETs) | 2 × 50 nC × 10 V × 48 k | 0.048 W (dissipated mostly in driver and R_g) |
| **Total** | | **≈ 1.71 W per channel** |

### 2.2 Total per-channel and full-ESC loss

$$P_{ch} = 22.3 + 1.7 \approx \mathbf{24\ W}$$

- **Per channel:** about 24 W.
- **All four motors at 80 A burst:** about 96 W.

### 2.3 Design levers

- **Conduction dominates (~93 %).** Lowering f_sw buys little; lowering R_ds(on) or paralleling FETs is what matters.
- **Dead time is the largest switching term.** Trimming t_dt from 100 ns to 50 ns saves about 0.3 W per channel.
- **Paralleling FETs** is the strongest lever. Two FETs per position halve conduction loss to about 11 W per channel. This is not feasible on a nano footprint.

---

## 3. Thermal Model

### 3.1 Steady state: not achievable at 80 A per channel

The thermal resistance from board to ambient for a 30×30 mm board in prop wash is roughly 4–8 K/W. With 96 W total:

$$\Delta T_{ss} \approx 96\times5 = 480\ \text{K}$$

**80 A per channel is strictly a burst rating.**

### 3.2 Burst: adiabatic lumped-capacitance model

Heat capacity of the board:

| Element | Calculation | Heat capacity |
|---|---|---|
| Copper | 9.3 cm² × 70 µm × 6 layers = 0.39 cm³ → 3.5 g × 0.385 J/g·K | 1.34 J/K |
| FR-4 | 1.49 cm³ → 2.75 g × 1.1 J/g·K | 3.0 J/K |
| Components and solder | estimate | ~0.6 J/K |
| **Total C_th** | | **≈ 5 J/K** |

The board temperature rise over a burst of length t is:

$$\Delta T_{board}(t) = \frac{P}{C_{th}}\,t\ \ (\text{adiabatic, } t \ll R_{th}C_{th}\approx25\,\text{s})$$

The junction sits above the board by:

$$T_j = T_{board} + P_{FET,pk}\cdot Z_{θJC}(t_p) \approx T_{board} + 11.1\times1.5 \approx T_{board}+17\ \text{K}$$

### 3.3 Burst budget

Limits: T_j,max = 150 °C, derated target 125 °C, ambient 35 °C. This gives a board temperature budget of about 108 °C, or **ΔT ≈ 73 K**.

| Load case | P | dT/dt | Time to limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 × 80 A | 96 W | 19 K/s | **≈ 3.8 s** |
| 1 × 80 A (punch-out on one arm, unusual) | 24 W | 4.8 K/s | ≈ 15 s |
| 4 × 40 A (realistic nano sustained peak) | ~26 W | 5.2 K/s | ≈ 14 s, then R_th-limited |

**Conclusion:** An honest nano 4-in-1 spec is about **40 A continuous / 80 A for ≤ 3 s per channel**, or **80 A total burst**. If marketing requires "80 A burst" per channel, you need one of the following:

- R_ds(on) ≤ 0.7 mΩ (5×6 mm packages, which will not fit 20×20 or 25.5 mm patterns).
- An aluminium heat spreader, which adds roughly 10–15 J/K.
- ESC firmware thermal foldback using the NTC (see §5).

### 3.4 Full transient expression

For tuning foldback, use:

$$T_{board}(t)=T_a+P R_{th}\left(1-e^{-t/R_{th}C_{th}}
